I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 40 years, and I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. My household has just two of us now, and with my family member working off-farm, I carry most of the field work myself. I have a well, so water is not my biggest worry — timing is.

For winter wheat, I will plant the full 10.1 mu in early October. I always use improved wheat varieties because the yield is stable and the grain quality is good. Before sowing, I will do rotary tillage to break up the stubble and prepare a fine seedbed — I’ve tried skipping this and the germination suffers. I will apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then topdress with urea at the jointing stage. Wheat needs water at critical times, so I will irrigate four times: once before winter to ensure safe overwintering, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice during the growing season, and fungicide once around heading to protect against powdery mildew and rust. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off the field in early June, I will plant hybrid maize seed directly into the wheat stubble without tillage — there is no time to waste between crops, and no-tillage keeps soil moisture. The area is the same 10.1 mu. I will apply compound fertilizer at planting. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat here; I will water twice — once if it turns dry right after sowing to ensure emergence, and again at the big flare stage. I will spray herbicide once, insecticide twice (especially for corn borer), and maybe a plant growth regulator once to prevent lodging. I expect around 560 kg per mu, which is typical for my field.

I stick with this wheat-maize rotation because it is what my land and my well can handle. I do not experiment much anymore — I know what works.
